title: Sticky affinity and degrade routing for canary variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need deterministic model version pinning for customers during canary/A-B rollouts while preserving region and tier routing policies and ensuring graceful degradation to fallback model variants when a chosen variant is unavailable. Current routing sometimes breaks session stickiness when requests are routed across regions or when autoscaling evicts nodes, causing inconsistent model versions for the same user/session and noisy evaluation signals.

Goal: Implement a sticky affinity mechanism that: 1) respects region selection and tier routing (paid/reserved vs shared), 2) supports configurable rollouts (percentage canaries, per-customer cohorts), 3) uses deterministic hashing for session-based pinning with TTL-based leases, and 4) provides explicit degrade paths to compatible model variants when the pinned variant is not reachable or fails SLOs.

Scope: Ingress routing layer changes (request-level resolver), routing metadata propagation (headers/tracing), server-side lease store for pinning, rollout weight manager, and metrics to validate stickiness and degrade events. This ticket focuses on the routing behavior and API/SDK compatibility contract; separate work will implement autoscaler integration and the Dedicated control-plane UI for releases.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic pinning: Requests with the same session_id and route config should map to the same model variant for the configured TTL across multiple backend restarts.

Region and tier precedence: Region selection and customer tier rules are applied before evaluating version pinning; pinned variants must respect region compatibility or trigger configured degrade policies.

Graceful degrade: If a pinned variant is unavailable, routing must fall back to a compatible variant according to a configurable priority list (e.g., quantized variant -> earlier stable version -> cross-region fallback) and emit a degrade event metric.
Observability: Per-request routing decisions logged with route_reason and variant_id; dashboards show stickiness ratio, degrade rate, and canary assignment distribution.
API contract: SDKs receive stable variant_headers for the duration of the TTL; clients see a header when degrade was applied and which variant was used.
E2E test: Canary rollouts with 10%, 50%, and 100% weights reproduce expected traffic split while retaining per-session stickiness in the presence of routing tier changes.
discussion: 2026-02-11: Initial design sketch posted in Confluence (link below). Raised question about whether pinning should be session-based (session_id header) or token-based (hash of user_id+route). Decided to support session_id as primary with fallback to deterministic request fingerprint.
2026-02-18: PM asked for per-customer override so enterprise customers can be force-pinned to a stable variant during their migration window. We added 'customer_affinity' flag to requirements.
2026-02-26: Spike completed: implemented a prototype lease store using the existing sticky-cookie table; prototype shows 99.98% stickiness across short outages in staging.
2026-03-02: Security review requested for header propagation and admin API to set override pins. Scoped to require audit logging; follow-up ticket for RBAC controls created.

2026-03-08: Discovered edge case: when region routing forces cross-region fallback, TTL must be shortened to avoid long-term cross-region traffic; decision to reduce TTL by half on cross-region degrade.
decisions: Use deterministic hashing of (customer_id|null, session_id|null, route_id) to assign sticky buckets. Bucket -> variant mapping computed by rollout manager.

Apply routing precedence: 1) customer_affinity overrides (enterprise pins), 2) region and tier filters, 3) rollout assignment (bucketed canary), 4) version pin lease lookup, 5) final degrade selection.
Lease semantics: leases stored with TTL (default 30 minutes) and refreshed on matching requests. Cross-region fallbacks set TTL to TTL/2 to reduce stale cross-region traffic.
Degrade priority: prefer same-architecture compatible quantized variants, then previous stable patch, then cross-region stable variant. Always emit a 'degrade' event with context for debugging.
Observability: include routing_reason and variant_id in trace/span tags; increment metrics routing.sticky_miss, routing.degrade_count, rollout.assignment_{variant}.
test_plan: Unit tests: hashing function, bucket assignment, and lease refresh behavior.
Integration tests: simulate region outage and verify degrade path and TTL adjustments.
Staging canary: ramp 5% -> 25% -> 75% while monitoring stickiness and customer-facing error rates; run synthetic traffic with per-session workloads.
Chaos test: kill nodes in a region to ensure leases and fallback behave correctly and that metrics surface degraded routing.
Manual QA: verify SDK receives variant headers and degrade header for three sample JS/Python clients.
notes: Implementation risk: lease store needs to be highly available and low latency; prefer colocated in control-plane region and replicate metadata instead of synchronous cross-region reads.
Backward compatibility: older SDKs that do not send session_id will use request fingerprinting; document behavior in SDK changelog.
Follow-ups: expose per-customer rollout admin UI, RBAC for enterprise forced pins, and autoscaler integration to prefer local variants during scale-down.
PR checklist: include migration plan for existing sticky-cookie table, integration test for TTL behavior, and update tracing instrumentation.
Owner: engineering runtime routing team; notify PM and design for console UX when rollout controls are surfaced.
